expressions.title: Civilisation, Its Cause and Cure
expressions.supporting_text: the oeuvre of the Socialist poet and philosopher, Edward Carpenter (1844-1929), whose work Civilisation, Its Cause and Cure (1889) has become the Bible of the social movements.

expressions.title: Mother Earth News
expressions.supporting_text: According to a historian of the eco‑village movement (Bates 2003) the magazine called Mother Earth News (Hendersonville, North‑California) started to set up organic gardens and energy saving houses next to their offices in 1975, which also functioned as education centres, and they started to call themselves eco‑village from 1979 on.

significance.justification: The magazine acted as a visible platform that framed and disseminated eco‑village concepts.
significance.supporting_text: Mother Earth News (Hendersonville, North‑California) started to set up organic gardens ... and they started to call themselves eco‑village from 1979 on.

expressions.title: In Context
expressions.supporting_text: Robert and Diane Gilman in their paper called In Context (Seattle) commenced to report on this and similar initiatives at the turn of the 1980s‑1990s.

significance.justification: The paper argued that such initiatives may serve as a model for sustainable ways of life, highlighting their systemic relevance.
significance.supporting_text: "In Context (Seattle) ... believed such initiatives may serve as a model for sustainable ways of life."

expressions.title: Global Ecovillage Network (GEN)
expressions.supporting_text: The international network, Global Ecovillage Network (GEN) was launched in 1994, in which the Hungarian Gyűrűfű project has already been involved as one of the funding members.

significance.justification: GEN is described as a network that coordinated projects and spread the eco‑village idea internationally.
significance.supporting_text: "The international network, Global Ecovillage Network (GEN) was launched in 1994... facilitating the propagation of the movement."

expressions.title: Danish eco‑village network
expressions.supporting_text: In 1993 the Danish eco‑village network was set up, the first of this kind, which later served as a model for the later launched international eco‑village movement.

significance.justification: It was the first of its kind and later served as a model for the later international eco‑village movement.
significance.supporting_text: "In 1993 the Danish eco‑village network was set up, the first of this kind, which later served as a model for the later launched international eco‑village movement."

expressions.title: Local Agenda 21 award
expressions.supporting_text: In 2004, ZEGG won the "Local Agenda 21" award set up by the regional administration of Potsdam-Mittelmark in the state of Brandenburg for the ensemble of its ecological work in the region.

significance.justification: The award symbolises official recognition, raising the profile of recipient ecovillages.
significance.supporting_text: ZEGG won the “Local Agenda 21” award set up by the regional administration...

expressions.title: National Agency for Ecovillages
expressions.supporting_text: The most striking recent breakthrough has been the decision by the government of Senegal to create a National Agency for Ecovillages.

significance.justification: Institutionalises ecovillage principles at national scale, opening pathways for systemic transformation.
significance.supporting_text: the decision by the government of Senegal to create a National Agency for Ecovillages.

expressions.title: Ecodyfi initiative
expressions.supporting_text: The Centre for Alternative Technology, a founding member of the GEN, is a leading player in the Ecodyfi initiative in Wales, an effort that brings together local authorities, the Welsh Assembly, various community groups, and specialist organizations with the mission "to foster sustainable community regeneration in the Dyfi valley".

significance.justification: Brings together multiple public and community actors to co‑design sustainable regeneration.
significance.supporting_text: Ecodyfi initiative in Wales, an effort that brings together local authorities, the Welsh Assembly, various community groups...

expressions.title: Save Our Water Now campaign
expressions.supporting_text: More than thirty years ago, its Save Our Water Now campaign organized local groups to stop deep-well injection into a regional aquifer by pesticide and herbicide companies.

significance.justification: Organised local groups to prevent environmental harm, exemplifying grassroots collective action.
significance.supporting_text: its Save Our Water Now campaign organized local groups to stop deep‑well injection into a regional aquifer...

expressions.title: Big Swan Headwaters Preserve
expressions.supporting_text: Its Big Swan Headwaters Preserve drew together local conservation organizations, state and local governments, and international charities like Nature Conservancy to protect more than three thousand contiguous acres from logging, subdivision, and development.

significance.justification: Coordinated diverse stakeholders to protect a large tract of land, showing networked action.
significance.supporting_text: Its Big Swan Headwaters Preserve drew together local conservation organisations, state and local governments, and international charities...

expressions.title: Peace Roots
expressions.supporting_text: The Farm has also organized an antiwar network--Peace Roots--that aligns veterans, farmers, students, and the general public in campaigns to oppose continued war spending.

significance.justification: Creates a cross‑sector anti‑war network, mobilising varied constituencies around a common cause.
significance.supporting_text: The Farm has also organized an antiwar network—Peace Roots—that aligns veterans, farmers, students, and the general public...

expressions.title: UN CIFAL training center
expressions.supporting_text: Today, the ecovillage hosts a UN CIFAL training center (one of eleven such centers worldwide), which provides sustainability-related training for local governments and other local actors.

significance.justification: Provides capacity‑building for local governments and actors, enabling broader implementation of sustainability practices.
significance.supporting_text: the ecovillage hosts a UN CIFAL training center … which provides sustainability‑related training for local governments...

expressions.title: La Caravana Arcoiris por la Paz (Rainbow Caravan of Peace)
actors: La Caravana Arcoiris por la Paz
expressions.supporting_text: La Caravana Arcoiris por la Paz (the Rainbow Caravan of Peace), a community of artists and ecological activists that have toured Latin America for the last ten years in a caravan of buses teaching sustainability through the arts.

significance.justification: Travels across Latin America delivering sustainability education through arts, mobilising communities.
significance.supporting_text: La Caravana Arcoiris por la Paz … have toured Latin America for the last ten years … teaching sustainability through the arts.

expressions.title: La Caravana commission by Brazilian government (development of fifty community‑based cultural centers)
actors: La Caravana Arcoiris por la Paz
expressions.supporting_text: Between 2005 and 2008, La Caravana was commissioned by the Brazilian government to help develop fifty community-based cultural centers in Brazilian towns and villages.

significance.justification: Government commissioning enables large‑scale cultural‑center creation, mobilising resources and participants.
significance.supporting_text: La Caravana ... was commissioned by the Brazilian government to help develop fifty community‑based cultural centers in Brazilian towns and villages.

expressions.title: Gaia University
expressions.supporting_text: university students are gaining credits from conventional universities for semesters spent in ecovillages (see Greenberg, Chapter 15, this volume) and degrees from ecovillage‑based institutes through the recently organized Gaia University.

significance.justification: Provides formal education pathways that build capacity for sustainability practice.
significance.supporting_text: university students are gaining credits ... and degrees from ecovillage‑based institutes through the recently organized Gaia University.

expressions.title: UN Habitat Scroll of Honor
expressions.supporting_text: In 2009, Sarvodaya was awarded the United Nations' prestigious UN Habitat Scroll of Honor in special recognition of its achievements in helping communities recover from the effects of the tsunami.

significance.justification: The award symbolises high‑level recognition, enhancing the perceived credibility of recipients.
significance.supporting_text: Sarvodaya was awarded the United Nations’ prestigious UN Habitat Scroll of Honor...

expressions.title: Right Livelihood Award
expressions.supporting_text: For its work in protecting indigenous cultures of the Americas through Plenty, The Farm received the first Right Livelihood Award, presented in the Swedish parliament in Stockholm.

significance.justification: The award signals global endorsement of sustainable practices.
significance.supporting_text: The Farm received the first Right Livelihood Award, presented in the Swedish parliament in Stockholm.

expressions.title: Gaia Education curriculum
expressions.supporting_text: Gaia Education has developed an educational curriculum drawn from best practice within ecovillages globally. ... The curriculum, developed by educators based in ecovillages around the world, has been endorsed by the United Nations Institute for Training and Research (UNITAR) and welcomed by the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation (UNESCO) as a valuable contribution to its UN Decade of Education for Sustainable Development.

significance.justification: The curriculum is taught worldwide, building capacity for sustainability action.
significance.supporting_text: Gaia Education has developed an educational curriculum drawn from best practice within ecovillages globally.

expressions.title: UN Decade of Education for Sustainable Development
expressions.supporting_text: The curriculum ... has been ... welcomed by the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation (UNESCO) as a valuable contribution to its UN Decade of Education for Sustainable Development.

significance.justification: Linking the curriculum to this UN decade raises its profile and policy relevance.

expressions.title: Master's program (Gaia Education curriculum)
expressions.supporting_text: The course is now being taught in ecovillages, universities, and community centers on every continent and has been taught virtually for several years through the Open University of Catalunya in Spain, where it is now offered as a master's program.

significance.justification: The master’s program trains professionals, expanding the movement’s human resources.

expressions.title: Future Scenarios
expressions.supporting_text: David Holmgren's Future Scenarios provides some insights into how the near- to medium-term future may unfold and the likely relevance of initiatives that are based on ecological design principles, such as ecovillages (Holmgren 2009).

significance.justification: The scenarios map possible future pathways, informing strategic choices.
